- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline (especially > -0.67 change), model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast by 5–15% in next 3–5 days.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment (e.g., +1.00 or +0.67), model often overcorrects — forecast should be capped at 10–15% below peak for 2–4 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (avg < 0.33) or news volume drops below 2.0, model tends to underestimate — add 3–8% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in sentiment-driven trends — if sentiment swings >0.50 from recent mean, adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment changes >0.50 in last 3–5 days, adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- When news volume is high (≥3.0) and sentiment is volatile, model tends to overfit — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day average) to reduce noise in forecast.
